title.narrative: SSD015N South Sudan JR 2021

description.promeva:title: Description (English)
description.narrative: Focusing on improving food security, nutrition and protection for conflict-affected communities in Koch (Unity State), the SSJR 7 project will provide emergency livelihood inputs, strengthen VSLA groups, raise awareness on CP and GBV and provide PSS through Child-Friendly Spaces and Women and Girls Friendly spaces. Nutrition activities include outreach, mobilisation, preventive and curative services to children < 5 and pregnant and lactacting women.

title.narrative: Nutrition - output
Number of people screened for under nutrition

comment.narrative: 4656 children of 6-59 months were screened for malnutrition during using MUAC tape as per the SSJR standards for conducting quarterly mass screening. Children who were severely or moderately malnourished were referred for admission to OTP and TSFP program.

A total of 13802 children and PLW (were screened for malnutrition using the MUAC tap, 7628 were normal (green), 5767 moderately malnourished (yellow) and 207 severely malnourished (red). Those severely or moderately malnourished were referred to OTP and TSFP programmes.
The activity was timely achieved. 137.4% (25,596: F=17,310, M=8,286; <18=15,886, >18=9,710) children and PLW were screened for malnutrition using the MUAC tap.

title.narrative: Number of children under 5 admitted for treatment of Severe or Moderate Acute Malnutrition

comment.narrative: . A total of 25596 (F=17310, M=8286; <18=15886, >18=9710) individuals were screened and 56.046% (2216: F= 1248, M=968, <18= 2216) children under 5 were admitted for treatment of Severe or Moderate Acute Malnutrition at the 3 Nutrition Centers for treatment of acute malnutrition.
1188 severely and moderately malnourished children were admitted to the nutrition programs of Jahjah, Bang, Jahjah and Petpet for treatment of acute malnutrition.
551 severely and moderately malnourished children were admitted to the nutrition programs of Jahjah, Bang, Jahjah and Petpet for treatment of acute malnutrition.

title.narrative: Number of pregnant or lactating women admitted for treatment of Severe or Moderate Acute Malnutrition

comment.narrative: 112% (2,304: (PW=1,077, LW=1,227) pregnant and lactating women were admitted to TSFP program for treatment. These PLWs were also enrolled to Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition activities and they join the mother to mother support groups during the bi-weekly meetings.
1181 pregnant and lactating women were admitted to the TSFP program for treatment .

695 females under 18 were admitted to the TSFP program for treatment. These PLWs are also enrolled to MIYCN activities and bi-weekly mother-to-mother support groups and Maternal and Infant Young Care Nutrition (MIYCN) counselling sessions focusing on nutrition sensitive interventions and targeting pregnant and lactating women with children under 24 months.

title.narrative: Number of health facilities where nutrition programmes are implemented

comment.narrative: CARE South Sudan continued to strengthen the 3 nutrition centers (Bang, Petpet & Jahjah) to effectively scale up equitable, evidence-based nutrition interventions and provide robust data including on MIYCN.
CARE continues to implement the nutrition programme in Petpet, Jahjah and Bang, offering outpatient therapeutic programme (OTP) and targeted supplementary feeding program (TSFP)

title.narrative: Protection - output
Number of persons reached by the implementation of specific GBV prevention measures

comment.narrative: 1128 individuals reached with EMAP activities in the 5 Bomas ( Jahjah, Petpet, Jaak, Bang and Koat). The EMAP process started with the deification of the facilitators and EMAP training.
CARE SS introduced a new activity “Engage Men through Accountable Practice (EMAP) to Prevent Violence Against Women and Girls” within the WGFS and CFS.

CARE introduced an new activity "Engage men through accountable practice (EMAP) to prevent violence against women and girls"within the WGFs and CFSs. The EMAP process started with sensitization of community leaders, selection and training of facilitators and training of target groups/communities. 16 EMAP groups have been formed (7 female and 9 male groups).

title.narrative: Number of children that received support specified to their needs

comment.narrative: 1625 children were reached with recreational activities at the CFSs of Bang, Jaak, Kuachlual and Petpet

4039 children were reached with recreational activities at the CFSs of Bang, Jaak, Kuachlual and Petpet with recreational, life skills and PSS such as drama, signing and dancing, drawing, storytelling, sports and playing games.

The activity was only partially achieved due to the flooding which dispalced some of the residents in the project sites. Child Friendly Spaces (CFSs) like Jahjah where not accessible as a result of flooding. Overal, the routine activities at CFSs were scaled down.

title.narrative: Number of participants showing an increased knowledge on the protection subject in focus

comment.narrative: 17 benefitted from case management training. The training is planned for 3 sessions to ensure social distancing and the subsequent trainings are planned for May 2021. The objectives of the training were: to support field-based delivery of quality survivor-centred, age-appropriate, GBV prevention, mitigation and response that meet global minimum services, as well as building capacity of frontline workers.

40 target individuals benefitted from GBV case management training. The 3-day training involved case workers, social workers, community facilitators/volunteers, mother-to-mother support groups, PMCs, police, local and religious leaders and youth leaders.

The activity was partially achieved because the expected number of particiapnts (60) did not all show up for the training, only 91.67 % of the participants representing (55, F= 24, M=31, <18=0, >18= 55) turned up for the training on GBV case management training.

title.narrative: Number of survivors who receive an appropriate response to GBV

comment.narrative: 25 GBV survivors received an appropriate GBV response and case management. These GBV survivors included rape (4), physical assault (14), forced marriage (4) and psychological/emotional abuse (5).

CARE SS provided case management to GBV survivors while applying survior centered approach. 131% (131: F=131,M=0. <18=30, >18=101) of originally targeted survivors received an appropriate response to GBV services such as case management.

CARE provided case management to GBV survivors based on a survivor-centered approach. 39 GBV survivors received an appropriate GBV response and case management. These GBV survivors included rape (4), physical assault (23), forced marriage (5) and psychological/emotional abuse (7).

title.narrative: Number of persons who receive an appropriate response

comment.narrative: 104% (11,514: F= 11,514, M=0, <18=2,094, >18=9,420) individuals were reached with PSS and resilience programs at the WGFS and CFSs. Due to the sporadic Inter-Communal Violence (ICV) and cattle raids, women and girls continue to be exposed, assaulted and suffer from GBV/CP concerns in the hands of the perpetuators.

5556 individuals were reached with PSS activities such as bead and bedsheet making, fuel efficient stove distribution, hair dressing, games (skipping ropes, throwing plates and valley balls) and traditional songs and dances which provided trauma healing to the GBV survivors at the WGFs.

5970 individuals were reached with PSS and resiliance programs at the WGFs and CFSs. Due to sporadic cattle raids, women and girls continue to be exposed to the risk of assault and GBV/CP concerns remain. CARE and UNIDOR have been monitoring response services for survivors and PSS and resilience activities.

title.narrative: Number of persons with increased/appropriate information on relevant rights and/or entitlements

comment.narrative: 102.24% (30,083: F= 19,611, M= 10,472, <18= 11,607, >18= 18,476.) individuals were reached with GBV/CP awareness raising sessions that were conducted in the communities (Jahjah, Petpet, Gap, Koat and Bang Bomas), targeting women, girls and men and boys through use of GBV Information educational materials (posters, banners, leaflets etc.) and focus group discussions.
21755 individuals were reached with GBV/CP awareness raising messaging in the target communities of Jahjah, Petpet, Gap, Koat abd Bang Bomas.
6983 individuals were reached with awareness raising messaging on the GBV/CP and risk communication and community engagement on COVID-19 preventive measures.

comment.narrative: CARE SS with its national partners continue to strengthen accountability with the established AAP system comprising of the Project Management Committees, the new formed Community Accountability Committee, the AAP Committee. Participation of the beneficiaries in project design, planning, implementation and monitoring and evaluation has been supported.

CARE SS with its national partners continue to strengthen accountability with the established AAP system comprising of the Project Management Committees, the new formed Community Accountability Committee, the AAP Committee. Participation of the beneficiaries in project design, planning, implementation and monitoring and evaluation has been supported.

CARE SS with its national partners continue to strengthen the accountability with the established AAP system which comprised of the 30 (F=7, M=23, >18=30) project management committees, the new formed Community Accountability Community (20: F= 15, M=5, >18=20), the AAP Committee (CARE =2, HDC=2, UNIDOR =1) and the beneficiaries to ensure the participation of the beneficiaries in project design, planning, implementation and monitoring and evaluation.

title.narrative: Number of adaptations in the design and/or implementation of the JR, as a result of the input from beneficiaries

comment.narrative: Through the PMCs, beneficiaries have been participating in the project design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of key aspects. This includes liaising with Payam authorities for the allocation og land for the Jaak WGF following the flood, participating in the provision of construction materials for the health facility in Jahjah, participation in feasibility studies for seed and tool preferences and the establishment of demo plots and kitchens at WGFs.

Through the PMCs, 12 adaptations have been incorporated in the programme during the implementation, including: participation during the feasibility studies for the project supplies such as FSl inputs, PSS materials, selection and setting up of the 10 demo gardens, site selection for the IGA shelters and selection of the sites for the CFSs among others.

title.narrative: Food Security & Livelihoods - output
Number of people provided with resources to protect and start rebuilding livelihood assets

comment.narrative: The activity was achieved in the mid-term. 10,800 (F=8,592, M=2,208, <18=9,36, >18=9,864) individuals were registered and provided with FSL inputs.

Through the PMCs, HDC registered 10800 individuals for the FSL inputs pending distribution of the seeds and tools which are expected to be delivered in Koch before the end of April 2021. The beneficiaries include the PWD, elderly, female-headed households, IDPs, returnees and the host community across the 3 Payams of Jaak ( Jahjah, Gaap, Petpe Bomas), Kuachlual (Koat Boma) and Gany (Bang Boma) Payam. The process began with feasibility studies for seed preference availability.

Through the PMCs, HDC registered 10800 individuals for the FSL inputs. The FSL inputs (seeds + tools) have been distributed in a timely manner and seeds have been planted. VSLAs have benefitted from strengthening of capacity and some have progressed to IGAs.

title.narrative: Localisation - output
Percentage of budget that went to national and local actors

comment.narrative: 10% (66834 Euro: HDC=43425 Euro, UNIDOR= 23409 Euro) of the budget went to the national partners for Q1 and the subsequent budget will be transferred to the national partners as per the partnership agreements.
31% ( of the budget went to the national partners (HDC=21%, UNIDOR 10%)

31% (HDC= 21%, UNIDOR=10%) of the budget was planned for the NNGOs. This budget covered the food security and livelihoods and child protection activities implemented by the local partners. 100% of the budget was transferred to them for their activities.

title.narrative: Percentage of budget spent on capacity building of national an local actors

comment.narrative: This particular activity is planned in the next quarter

UNIDOR conducted an organizational needs assessment using the CAT template and institutional capacity strengthening was identified as the priority need. The gaps identified were lack of furniture for the staff/care takers at CFS. Based on the needs identified, UNIDOR procured furniture and some basic playing materials like foot balls for CFS.

UNIDOR conducted organizational needs assessments using the CAT template and institutional capacity strengthening was identified as the priority need. Based on the needs assessment UNIDOR procured equipment such as furniture, basic playing materials (e.g. footballs) for CFS. Equipment was distributed to 5 locations: Mirmir, Bhang, Kuachlual, Jaak and Jahjah CFS, as well as the Koch office.

title.narrative: Number of national and local actors supported with capacity-building

comment.narrative: This particular activity is planned in the next quarter
UNIDOR conducted trainings on case management and reached 42 individuals (F=25, M= 17; all 18+). Participants were stakeholders and service providers in Mirmir and Koch (kuachlual)

UNIDOR, HDC and line ministries and PMCs benefitted from the capacity buidling which included human and institutional capacity strengthening. The institutional capacity strengthening that benefitted the local actors including the provision of plastic chair and tables as per their needs.
